captions.text: Recap of chapter 17: you wrapped one model in another.
Retry tries again after a temporary failure, and Fallback uses another model.
LoopGuard stops the same tool call repeating, again and again.
None of them fixes a confident wrong answer. So did they help?
Today's black box: how to measure an agent.
Let's open it.
First, the slow way. Ask the coffee question five times, and read each answer.
Predict: how many of the five will be right?
Five out of five, this time. You were the check: you looked for 380.
Five questions, two agents, every change. Nobody reads 50 answers twice.
So the marking becomes code. A Check is a label and a test.
Callable means a function. It takes a Result, and says True or False.
lambda writes a small function in one line, with no name.
A Case is one question and the checks its answer must pass.
run_eval runs it five times. A run passes only if every check passes.
Five of five. Steps is the average number of model calls.
Failed runs are kept, with their answers. There are none here.
Can you trust a check? Try one on answers we wrote ourselves. No model needed.
Predict: which of these will contains get wrong?
It passes 1,380 and 3800, and it fails the right answer written in words.
Your eval measures your checks as well as your agent.
Now five cases, on two agents: the plain model, and chapter 17's safety nets.
Predict: will the safety nets raise the score?
Plain scored 23 of 25, and reliable scored 25. Two cases gained one each.
It's tempting to say the safety nets worked. Hold on.
Test the test. Run the same agent, round after round, and change nothing.
Predict: how far will the score move?
From 21 to 25, with nothing changed. So 23 and 25 are both normal.
A difference means nothing unless it's bigger than an agent against itself.
Now the reliable agent, also six rounds.
146 of 150, against 141 for plain. The ranges nearly match. It's not proof.
But all 4 of its failures had the right total. They just skipped add_numbers.
Plain had 6 runs with no right answer. Read the failures, not just the score.
Some things have no number to check. So ask a model to grade: an LLM judge.
A judge can be wrong too. Test it on six answers we marked by hand.
It matched 5 of 6, and our simple code check matched 2.
But it passed "probably about 127". Prefer code when code can do the job.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You'll write a stricter number check, and more. No Ollama needed.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
